# Controlled known-item retrieval corpus

Six equivalent thermal-feedback ideas exercise the real reviewed-plan/native
retrieval/adaptive/fusion engine with synthetic HTTP responses. Expected identities
are declared separately from responses. Recordings selectively hide known work
from one path and expose it through another: lexical, native semantic, alternate
corpus, predecessor references, adjacent domain, or an explicit translated query.
Every query runs through the actual compiler and provider adapter.

The translated case supplies French text explicitly; it does not implement a
translator or claim multilingual research coverage. No LLM or live search quality
is being measured. Recovery paths retain their query or seed and provider rank.
Metrics operate within the control MCU's scholarly objective, not across unrelated
claims/families. Recall@K is binary for each designated known item; reciprocal rank
records its first fused position. These are retrieval metrics, not novelty scores.

`baseline.json` records the observed Phase 4 synthetic distribution, including the
mechanism case's rank-2 predecessor. It is not a universal production threshold
or a live-corpus performance estimate. Tests require recovery and the intended
path classes; no flaky live metric gates deterministic CI.
